svg.text: How the System Works — From Word List & Dice to 1 Million Boards (Left → Right)
Visual Guide to Data Layout, Shuffling & Multi-Core Scaling
Words share common prefix paths in a tree:
Naive Node: 26 Slots per Node (112 Bytes)
47.9 MB total — too big for fast CPU cache
How a Node Finds Its Child in 8 Bytes (3.49 MB Total)
Node "CA" stores a 26-bit mask (1 bit per letter A..Z)
plus the index of its first child (100):
To jump to 'T': count '1' bits before 'T' (popcount = 2):
Rules baked in: 'Q' jumps straight to "QU" · Words < 3 letters unmarked
Keep Word Text Separate (So Nodes Stay Tiny)
Nodes don't store strings; found words look up a 4-byte span:
Only read at the end for the few words actually found!
Threads grab the next batch as soon as they finish
• Keeps its own reusable scratch memory:
• Reuses memory buffers across all boards:
Instead of allocating for all 138,735 dictionary
words up front (17.7 MB across 32 threads),
each thread starts with a tiny 4 KB buffer
that fits inside the CPU's fastest L1 cache.
